tests.prompt:
Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: no.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

Corner radius: 12px - Soft - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

Corner radius: Full - Pill - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.

- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Large - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

Corner radius: 0px - Sharp - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Large - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. Test collision and zoom; do not infer stacking order from shadow size."}

### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Small - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

Portal menus out of clipped scroll containers. Nested dialogs stack one scrim per modal owner. Escape closes the top dismissible layer. Tooltips never block actions. ### Acceptance still required

- Compare page, applied tokens, durable record, Machine View and exported instructions.
- Test valid, unfinished, invalid, missing, malformed, legacy and future records. Exercise storage failure, reset, reload and another tab.
- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.
- Verify actual rendered text/surface pairs, forced colors, reduced motion, print and exported recipes in a recipient fixture. Source or DOM checks alone are not rendered acceptance.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

Size: Middle - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option. Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

## Implementation contract

Saved validated choices override project recommendations, which override system defaults. This implementation contract governs static specimens. Resolved tokens in the current export are authoritative values. Component exceptions must name the affected role and reason.

### Ownership and compatibility

- owners: Design System Lead owns token and compatibility policy. Designers own specimens and interaction contracts. Developers own resolver/export/import parity. QA and Accessibility own release evidence. Product teams own domain-specific confidence, privacy and retention policies.
- changes: Change the JSON contract first, regenerate documentation/defaults/catalog/tokens, then run model, DOM and recipient checks. Link the changed finding IDs and evidence in the release review.
- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

### Units

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
- Prefer rem for typography, spacing and control dimensions. Hairline borders and viewport thresholds may use px. Both equivalents appear in Markdown. SVG strokes use viewBox units. Ratios, percentages, columns, timing and weights are unitless or retain their own units.
- Web CSS px/rem are not native dp/sp. A native adapter must map semantic roles, support text scaling and test device density. Native rendering is not shipped by this web library.

### Layers

- Test 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px widths, 200% zoom, text-spacing overrides, RTL and long/localized labels.
- Use keyboard and screen reader. Confirm focus return, names, values, error associations and status announcements.

Create a complete Table component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, corner radius, size, show header) - a structured grid of rows and columns for displaying tabular data (Name / Status / Role / Email / Mobile example columns - Email and Mobile render as real mailto:/tel: links, styled in this system's defined link color, var(--red-400)), with a header row and optional cell borders, alternating row stripes, or row selection.

Border styles (2):
- Default: Minimal - only a bottom border under the header row and thin row-separator lines, no outer border or vertical cell lines.
- Bordered: A full grid - outer border plus vertical and horizontal lines between every cell, like a spreadsheet.

States (5, apply to the whole set of body rows at once):
- Default: Plain rows - no striping, no selection.
- Striped: The same rows, but every other row gets a subtly different background for alternating-row legibility.
- Selected: The same rows, now each with a leading checkbox column - the first row is visually marked as selected with a red-tinted row background and a checked checkbox, the other two rows show unchecked checkboxes.
- Loading: The same row count and column count, but every cell replaced with a Skeleton placeholder bar - so the table's shape doesn't jump once the real rows arrive.
- Empty: No rows at all - a single spanning cell showing the Empty component (icon, title, description) instead of a blank body, so a zero-result search reads as a real answer, not a rendering failure.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to the Bordered type's outer container only - the Default type never carries a radius.

What size do you want? (Small / Middle / Large) Scales cell padding only - column widths and font-size stay the same at every size.

Component properties: Corner radius (Bordered type only); Size; Show header (boolean, default checked - shows the column-label header row above the body rows).
Current values - Show header: yes.

Interaction contract (real, data-backed usage, beyond this page's static demos):
- Selection (3): None / Single-row / Multi-row (checkbox column).
  - None: Rows aren't selectable - no checkbox column, no row highlight on click.
  - Single-row: Clicking a row selects it exclusively, like a radio group - selecting a new row clears the previous selection.
  - Multi-row (checkbox column): A leading checkbox column, one checkbox per row plus a header checkbox that selects/deselects every visible row. When some but not all visible rows are checked, the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked. Space toggles selection on a focused row.
- Sort: Client-side sort re-orders already-loaded rows in memory - fine for small, fully-loaded datasets. Server-side sort re-requests the current page/window from the server on every sort change - required once pagination or virtualization is server-driven. Single-column sort is the default; multi-column sort (shift-click a header to add a secondary sort key) is an opt-in advanced behavior, not required of every implementation. Per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages), a sortable header must expose its state via aria-sort="ascending|descending|none" and announce the change to assistive technology, not just show a visual arrow icon.
- Filter: A per-column filter, scoped to just that field (e.g. a status dropdown in the Status header). A global search bar above the table, matching across every visible column at once. A "no rows match" empty state (rows exist, the current filter/search matched none of them - offer a Clear filters action) must read differently from the true empty state (no data exists at all - offer a create action).
- Pagination vs virtualization (threshold 500 rows): Below 500 rows, client-side pagination (or simply rendering every row) is fine - the DOM cost is small and bounded. At or above 500 rows, virtualization (windowed rendering - only rows in or near the viewport are ever mounted) is required, since a table row is not a cheap DOM node and DOM/layout cost does not scale linearly with row count past a few hundred rows.
- Density (2): Comfortable - The default row height and cell padding. Compact - Reduced row height and cell padding, for scanning more rows in the same viewport height.
- Required states (3): Empty (no data at all) - Reuses the Empty component (icon, title, description) plus a call-to-action, never a header with a silently blank body. Loading - Skeleton rows matching the real column count, not a blank table and not the empty-state message. Error - A failed fetch shows what went wrong plus a Retry action, never silently falling back to the same empty state as a true zero-result answer.

- compatibility: Keep hue-named CSS tokens as compatibility aliases while semantic consumers migrate. Additive tokens retain schemaVersion 1. A removed/renamed key or changed stored meaning requires a schema migration, a version bump and a documented replacement before release. Keep the prior reader fixture until the migration is verified.
- deprecation: Record old key, replacement, reason, introduced version, planned removal version and affected consumers. Do not remove a token while an active consumer still uses it. Future records are preserved rather than coerced.
- scope: This is a web design system with one shared workspace profile. Native dp/sp adaptation and real agent execution require separate adapters and acceptance. User-defined colors and responsive exceptions require product-specific rendered verification.

### Storage and recovery

- version: 1
- legacy: Unversioned valid records migrate in memory. Typography headingScaleVersion 2 applies the smaller six-heading scale once to older records, retaining other roles and existing font/color/style metrics. Later custom size edits are retained. Unsupported future records are preserved. The next successful write stamps the migrated version.
- future: Reject unsupported future versions. Preserve raw data. Offer backup and explicit reset.
- invalid: Keep unfinished drafts separate. Invalid drafts neither apply nor save. Storage failures retain an explicitly marked local preview and the last durable record.
- concurrency: A storage event refreshes applied tokens and disables stale editor controls until reload. Never merge simultaneous edits silently.

- 1rem = 16px at default browser settings. Do not fix the root font size.
